transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?
I came in because I barely want to eat anymore. At work on my lunch break, I’ll look at food I usually like, and I just end up throwing most of it away.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you been feeling persistently sad, down, or empty most of the day, nearly every day?
I'm not really sure. I haven't noticed feeling sad most of the day like that.
When you find yourself not wanting to eat, are you worried about gaining weight or concerned about how your body looks?
No, I don’t think it’s about my weight or how I look. I just don’t really feel like eating.
Did this loss of appetite start around the same time as any particular stressful event or major change in your life?
Yeah, I think so. It’s been about two months—since I got that window display award and the district manager started giving me all this attention.

Have you been feeling anxious or worried lately, and if so, is that worry mostly about the new attention and expectations at work, or do you find yourself worrying about many different things in your life?

Mostly about work. I keep thinking I must’ve copied some real artist for that display, even though my manager shows me the old Photoshop files and says it was mine. It still feels like people are quietly keeping notes on me until they can prove I stole it.

Even when your manager shows you the original files proving the design was yours, does that change how convinced you are that people are watching you, or do you still feel certain they're keeping notes on you regardless of what evidence you're shown?
No. I see the files, but it doesn’t really change it. I still feel like I must have copied it from some real artist somehow, and people at work are keeping track until they can prove it.
Since this feeling of being watched and accused started two months ago, has it been present continuously every day since then, or has it come and gone in shorter episodes with breaks in between?
It’s been there pretty much every day. I keep thinking I copied somebody’s work, and that people at work are keeping notes until they can prove it, even though my manager shows me the old files.
Aside from these thoughts about being watched, have you been able to keep up with your usual work tasks and daily routines, or has this been getting in the way of functioning normally?

I’m still going to work, but it’s been affecting me. I’ve messed up inventory counts and display plans enough that my manager has to double-check what I do. And I’ve stopped going to gallery nights, basketball, and the youth art workshops I used to go to.
When you look back, did these thoughts about being watched and accused come on suddenly over just a few days, or did they build up gradually over weeks?
I’m not really sure. I just know it’s been going on for a while now; I can’t say exactly how it started.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a single, fixed, non-bizarre persecutory delusion (belief that coworkers are monitoring him to 'prove' he plagiarized a design) that has persisted daily for approximately 2 months and remains unshaken by clear disconfirming evidence (manager showing original files). There is no evidence of hallucinations, disorganized speech, negative symptoms, or broader psychotic disorganization required for schizophrenia. Mood symptoms (pervasive sadness/emptiness) were explicitly denied, and the appetite change is attributable to preoccupation with the delusion rather than a primary mood or eating disorder, and there is no weight/body image concern ruling out anorexia nervosa. Functioning is relatively preserved except for delusion-related impairment (work errors, social withdrawal), consistent with Delusional Disorder rather than Schizophrenia, where functioning is more globally deteriorated and additional psychotic symptoms are present.
